Binding for every project of this folder (corpus.md). Echo tags follow guidelines §6.4: [cognate], [equivalent], [divergence], [absent]. Fixed by the corpus coordinator (Round 2, run 7, 2026-10-21) before the first line was drafted, from the earlier corpora (looked up by string and by lemma: kol_tools.py lookup, kol_tools.py grep all) and a survey of the three base texts (ORACC lemma frequencies; the formulas found in the transliterations). Translators propose additions in their project.md ("Proposals"); the coordinator merges them here (§9). The translator of a formula's first occurrence may revise a pre-set rendering of §3 with a reason; after that it binds and the script checks it.

0. Inheritance

  1. Akkadian (project 1): the Gilgameš corpus (../אפוס-גילגמש/renderings.md) binds first for love, body and household words – it already fixed kuzbu = עֲגָבִים, lalû = עֹנֶג, ḫabābu = חִבֵּק, dādū = דּוֹדִים (I 185 דודיו יחבקו אותך), râmu = אָהַב, ūru = עֶרְוָה, inbu = תְּנוּבָה (never פְּרִי), kirû = גַּן ("no garden word without kirû"), nukaribbu = גַּנָּן, mayyālu = מִשְׁכָּב, eršu = עֶרֶשׂ, sikkūru = בְּרִיחַ, rēʾû = רוֹעֶה, summatu = יוֹנָה, ṣabītu = צְבִיָּה, eṭlu / ardatu / ḫīrtu / aššatu / sinništu / marḫītu = עֶלֶם / עַלְמָה / כַּלָּה / אֵשֶׁת / אִשָּׁה / רַעְיָה, mutu = בַּעַל, aḫāzu "marry" = בָּעַל (here נָשָׂא by sense where the subject is the woman's family – see §3), damqu = נָאֶה, banû (adj.) = יָפֶה, tebû = קָם, dekû = הֵעִיר, lapātu = נָגַע, šittu = שֵׁנָה, šuttu = חֲלוֹם, ellu = טָהוֹר, mēlulu = חוּל / מָחוֹל, lillu = כְּסִיל, ṣēru = שָׂדֶה. Then the wisdom corpus (libbu לֵב, kabattu כָּבֵד, ilu "my god" אֵלִי ★, šiptu קֶסֶם – settled by the 2026-10-21 harmonization, §9), the flood corpus (ṣīḫtu = צְחוֹק, ṣiāḫu = צָחַק), the law corpus (kallatu = כַּלָּה, emu = חָם, awīlum = אִישׁ, wardum / amtum = עֶבֶד / אָמָה).
  2. Sumerian (projects 2–3): the temple, lament and creation corpora bind, most recent first (../בניין-המקדש/renderings.md, ../קינות-על-ערים/renderings.md, ../סיפורי-הבריאה-המסופוטמיים/renderings.md §5–§8): lu₂ = אָדָם (a person; אִישׁ where "a man" against a woman), uĝ₃ = עָם, kalam = הָאָרֶץ, e₂ = בַּיִת, iri = עִיר, dug₃ = טוֹב (reserved), sag₉ = נָאֶה, ḫul = רַע, ḫul₂ = שָׂמַח, gig = מַר, kur₂ = נָכְרִי / verb שִׁנָּה, lu₂-erim₂ = אוֹיֵב, gi₄ / gur = שׁוּב, in … dub₂ = חֵרֵף, aš₂ … bal = קִלֵּל, nam … ku₅ = אָרַר, nam tar = גָּזַר גּוֹרָל, nam-kug-zu = חָכְמָה, ĝeštug₂ = בִּינָה (also "ear" אֹזֶן by sense), galam = נוֹכֵל, ĝiškim = אוֹת ★, lamma = אֵלַת־מָגֵן, mušen = צִפּוֹר, dal = עָף, za-gin₃ = סַפִּיר, šembi = פּוּךְ, ra-gaba = צִיר ★, šudu₃ / sizkur₂ / a-ra-zu = בְּרָכָה / תְּפִלָּה / תַּחֲנוּן, guru₇ = כְּרִי, en₃-du = זִמְרָה (the 2026-10-21 harmonization, §9), ku₆ = דָּג, u₈ = רָחֵל, engar = אִכָּר, na-gada = נוֹקֵד, dam-gar₃ = תַּגָּר (= tamkāru), zid = נֶאֱמָן / אֱמֶת, me = הַ־מֶה ★. A Sumerian word takes the Hebrew of its Akkadian equivalent.
  3. Shared with the other Round 2 runs (run 5 ../העולם-התחתון/, run 6 ../אגדות-מלכים/; looked up on their disk folders before fixing, 2026-10-21 – they did not exist yet): Inana אִינַנָּה ★, Ištar אִשְׁתַּר, Dumuzi דּוּמוּזִי, Enki אֶנְקִי, Ea אֵאָה, Enlil אֶנְלִיל, Utu אוּתוּ ★, Šamaš שַׁמַשׁ, Nanna נַנָּה, Suen סוּאֵן, Sîn סִין ★, Ningal נִינְגַּל, Anu אָנוּ ★, An אַן ★, Nisaba נִיסַבָּה, Ninĝišzida נִינְגִּישְׁזִידָה, Išḫara אִשְׁחַרָה, Belili בֵּלִילִי ★ (run 5 fixed the same form, always vocalized: unvocalized בלילי = "in my night"), Nanaya נַנָּיָה (new), Uruk אוּרוּךְ, Nibru נִיפּוּר, Urim אוּר ★, Eridug אֶרִידוּ, Kiš כִּישׁ, Babylon בָּבֶל, Tigris חִדֶּקֶל, Dilmun דִּלְמוּן, the Igigi אִיגִיגִי, the Anunnaki אֲנוּנָּכִּי.

1. Names

Vocalized at the first occurrence in each annotated file; afterwards plain spelling, except ★, vocalized at every occurrence (unvocalized they read as Hebrew words; kol_tools.py verify checks them).

Source Hebrew Notes
Ištar; Nanaya; Muʾati (Nabû); Dumuzi; Ningal; Sîn ★; Anu(m) ★; Ea; Enki; Išḫara; Adad; Šamaš; Belili; Ninlil אִשְׁתַּר; נַנָּיָה; מוּאָתִי; דּוּמוּזִי; ★ סִין; ★ אָנוּ; אֵאָה; אֶנְקִי; אִשְׁחַרָה; אֲדַד; שַׁמַשׁ; בֵּלִילִי; נִינְלִיל Nanaya: a goddess of love, from Ur III on often a hypostasis of Ištar; Muʾati: her consort in OB Babylon, later identified with Nabû (note at first occurrence). סין unvocalized reads "China", אנו reads "we". Dumuzi = the biblical הַתַּמּוּז (יחזקאל ח:יד): note, never assimilated.
Kings: Rīm-Sîn; Abī-ešuḫ; Ammī-ditāna; Ammī-ṣaduqa; Šū-Sîn; Hammurabi רִים־★סִין; אֲבִי־אֶשׁוּחַ; עַמִּי־דִּיתָנָה; עַמִּי־צָדוּקָה; שׁוּ־★סִין; חַמּוּרַבִּי The kings for whom the songs were sung (Larsa, Babylon, Ur III).

People of the letters: Lu-diĝira; Šat-Eštar; Ugubi; Aba-taḫ-lugalĝa; Šamaš-ṭāb; Ilak-niʾid; Inanaka; Enlil-amaḫ; Inim-Inana; Enlil-massu; Lugal-ibila; Lu-gena; Ur-saga; Gudea לוּ־דִּינְגִּירָה; שַׁת־אֶשְׁתַּר; אוּגוּבִּי; אַבָּא־תַּח־לוּגַלְגָּה; שַׁמַשׁ־טָאב; אִילַק־נִיאִיד; אִינַנָּקָה; אֶנְלִיל־אַמַח; אִינִים־★אִינַנָּה; אֶנְלִיל־מַסּוּ; לוּגַל־אִיבִּילָה; לוּ־גֵּינָה; אוּר־שַׂגָּה; גּוּדֵאָה Vocalized at the first occurrence; the meaning of the name in the apparatus where it matters (Lu-diĝira "man of god"; Inim-Inana "word of Inana").

2. Grammar

  • Akkadian (guidelines §6.3; the Gilgameš and wisdom corpora): preterite = past; present = future / present by context; stative = adjective or nominal clause; precative lu-/li- = jussive / cohortative (אֶשְׂבְּעָה, יִשְׂבַּע); the ventive rendered when it means motion toward the speaker (בּוֹא אֵלַי); the dual and the plural of the body kept (šaptāki שְׂפָתַיִךְ); gender of the address kept (Hebrew distinguishes -ka / -ki as the Akkadian does: דֹּדֶיךָ / דֹּדַיִךְ – this is how the dialogues show who speaks).
  • Speakers of the dialogues (LAOS 4 01, 15, 16, 18): the tablet does not mark them; Wasserman's attribution (He:) / (She:) / (Chorus:) is an interpretation. In the > line: no speaker tags; in the apparatus: who speaks, and why (the gender of the verbs and suffixes).
  • Sumerian (creation corpus, lament corpus): ḫamṭu = past; marû = participle / future; ḫe₂- = jussive (or affirmative, by context: say so); ga- = cohortative; na- + marû = prohibition אַל; nu- = לֹא; the copula -am₃ = nominal sentence. Proverbs are timeless: a ḫamṭu in a proverb is often a gnomic past (the "it happened once" of a fable); render it as a past and say so where it is gnomic.

3. Key terms and formulas (pre-set; enforced by kol_tools.py verify where FORMULAS / RESERVED have a pattern)

3.1 Love (project 1)

Source Hebrew Tag / Bible Notes
dādu "darling, beloved"; pl. dādū "love-making, (sexual) love" דּוֹד (דּוֹדִי, דּוֹדָהּ); pl. דּוֹדִים (דֹּדֶיךָ, דֹּדַיִךְ, דֹּדָיו) [cognate] ↔ כִּי טוֹבִים דֹּדֶיךָ מִיָּיִן (שיר השירים א:ב); דּוֹדִי (שיר השירים ב:ח ...) Reserved: דוד only for dādu. Always vocalized (unvocalized דוד reads "David", דודים "uncles"). The Gilgameš corpus binds the plural (I 185).
râmu (verb); râmu / ruʾāmu (noun "love; love-charm"); rāʾimu "lover"; raʾīmu / rāmu / narāmu "beloved"; ritūmu (Gt) "love-making" אָהַב; אַהֲבָה; אוֹהֵב (f. אוֹהֶבֶת); אָהוּב (f. אֲהוּבָה); אֳהָבִים (vocalized) [equivalent] (law, Gilgameš); אֳהָבִים ↔ נִתְעַלְּסָה בָּאֳהָבִים (משלי ז:יח) Reserved: the root אהב only for the râmu family. ritūmu is the reciprocal Gt "mutual love(-making)": אֳהָבִים (the plural of love-making).
kuzbu; lalû; ṣīḫtu / ṣiāḫu עֲגָבִים; עֹנֶג; צְחוֹק / צָחַק Gilgameš; flood; ṣīḫtu [cognate] ↔ וְהִנֵּה יִצְחָק מְצַחֵק אֵת רִבְקָה אִשְׁתּוֹ (בראשית כו:ח) צחק reserved for the ṣiāḫu family: the erotic "laughter" of the songs is the cognate of Isaac's מְצַחֵק.
inbu (also sexual "fruit"); ḫašḫūru; kirû; nukaribbu; ṣēru תְּנוּבָה (pl. תְּנוּבוֹת); תַּפּוּחַ; גַּן; גַּנָּן; שָׂדֶה inbu [cognate] of אֵב / Aram. אִנְבֵּהּ (דניאל ד:ט), but תנובה binds; ḫašḫūru [equivalent] ↔ כְּתַפּוּחַ בַּעֲצֵי הַיַּעַר כֵּן דּוֹדִי (שיר השירים ב:ג); kirû [equivalent] ↔ גַּן נָעוּל (שיר השירים ד:יב) Reserved: תפוח only ḫašḫūru; גן only kirû (Sum. kiri₆); פרי never in project 1 (note the Song's פְּרִי in the apparatus).
dišpu; karānu / kurunnu; šamnu; ḫimētu; qutrinnu; erēnu; ballukku דְּבַשׁ; יַיִן / שֵׁכָר (see Sum. kaš); שֶׁמֶן; חֶמְאָה; קְטֹרֶת; אֶרֶז; בַּלּוּכּוּ (a fragrant plant, transliterated) dišpu [cognate] ↔ דְּבַשׁ וְחָלָב תַּחַת לְשׁוֹנֵךְ (שיר השירים ד:יא); šamnu [cognate] ↔ שֶׁמֶן תּוּרַק שְׁמֶךָ (שיר השירים א:ג); qutrinnu [cognate]; erēnu [cognate] Never in project 1 (the Song's own spices and flowers, with no counterpart here): שושנה, חבצלת, לבנון, מור, לבונה, נרד, כרכם, קנמון, צוף, תמר (unless gišimmaru).
šaptu; pû; īnu; irtu "breast"; tulû "breast"; sūnu "lap"; ūru "vulva"; qablu "waist"; šumēlu; imittu; lānu "figure"; zīmu שָׂפָה; פֶּה; עַיִן; חָזֶה; שַׁד; חֵיק; עֶרְוָה; מָתְנַיִם; שְׂמֹאל; יָמִין; קוֹמָה; מַרְאֶה šumēlu [cognate] ↔ שְׂמֹאלוֹ תַּחַת לְרֹאשִׁי וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי (שיר השירים ב:ו); lānu ↔ זֹאת קוֹמָתֵךְ דָּמְתָה לְתָמָר (שיר השירים ז:ח) [equivalent] The body is named as the tablet names it (guidelines §5.2 "describe as the original describes"); no euphemism.
ḫabābu "caress; murmur"; edēru "embrace"; našāqu "kiss"; niāku "have sex"; ṣalālu "lie, sleep"; nâlu "lie down" חִבֵּק (of water "murmur": הָמָה, the lemma noted); לָפַת; נָשַׁק; בָּא עַל (law corpus niāku = בא על); יָשַׁן; שָׁכַב חבק ↔ וִימִינוֹ תְּחַבְּקֵנִי (שיר השירים ב:ו) [equivalent – the Song's verb is Akk. edēru's sense; Gilgameš binds חבק to ḫabābu] Reserved: חבק only ḫabābu; לפת only edēru (wisdom); נשק only našāqu (or kakku "weapon").
tebû (imper. tibi / tibâ); alāku (imper. alik, ventive alkam / alkī); erēbu (imper. erub, erbam) קוּם / קוּמִי / קוּמָה; לֵךְ / לְכָה / לְכִי; בּוֹא / בּוֹאִי / בּוֹאָה [equivalent] ↔ קוּמִי לָךְ רַעְיָתִי יָפָתִי וּלְכִי לָךְ (שיר השירים ב:י); לְכָה דוֹדִי נֵצֵא הַשָּׂדֶה (שיר השירים ז:יב); יָבֹא דוֹדִי לְגַנּוֹ (שיר השירים ד:טז) Gated imperatives: קום… only tebû (Sum. zig₃, gana); לכה/לכי only alāku (Sum. ĝen, du); בוא/בואי/בואה only erēbu / bâʾu (Sum. ku₄).
mūšu; urru; šēru; mayyālu; eršu; daltu; sikkūru; aptu; nūru לַיְלָה; יוֹם; בֹּקֶר; מִשְׁכָּב; עֶרֶשׂ; דֶּלֶת; בְּרִיחַ; חַלּוֹן; אוֹר eršu [cognate] ↔ אַף עַרְשֵׂנוּ רַעֲנָנָה (שיר השירים א:טז); mayyālu [equivalent] ↔ עַל מִשְׁכָּבִי בַּלֵּילוֹת (שיר השירים ג:א); aptu [equivalent] ↔ מַשְׁגִּיחַ מִן הַחַלֹּנוֹת (שיר השירים ב:ט) מנעול (the Song's lock) never: sikkūru = בְּרִיחַ (Gilgameš).
rēʾû; ṣēnu; supūru; tarbaṣu; summatu; iṣṣūru; ṣabītu; ayyalu רוֹעֶה; צֹאן; דִּיר; רֶבֶץ; יוֹנָה; צִפּוֹר; צְבִיָּה; אַיָּל rēʾû [cognate] ↔ הַגִּידָה לִּי שֶׁאָהֲבָה נַפְשִׁי אֵיכָה תִרְעֶה אֵיכָה תַּרְבִּיץ בַּצָּהֳרָיִם (שיר השירים א:ז); summatu [equivalent] ↔ יוֹנָתִי בְּחַגְוֵי הַסֶּלַע (שיר השירים ב:יד) Reserved: יונה only summatu (Sum. tu-gur₄).
aḫātu; aḫu; ummu; abu; mārtu; māru; kallatu; ḫīrtu; emu; marḫītu; tappātu "girlfriend" אָחוֹת; אָח; אֵם; אָב; בַּת; בֵּן; כַּלָּה ★; כַּלָּה ★; חָם; רַעְיָה; רֵעָה aḫātu [cognate] ↔ אֲחֹתִי כַלָּה (שיר השירים ד:ט); marḫītu ↔ רַעְיָתִי [equivalent; Gilgameš binds רעיה] כלה vocalized (כַּלָּה) at every occurrence (unvocalized = "finished"). Reserved: רעיה only marḫītu.
ḫadû; ḫidûtu; riāšu; rīštu; elṣu / elṣiš; duššupu; matqu; ṭābu שָׂמַח; שִׂמְחָה; גָּל; גִּילָה; עַלִּיז / בַּעֲלִיזוּת; מְמֻתָּק; מָתוֹק; טוֹב (reserved) A deviation from the flood corpus (rīštum שמחה): this corpus has both ḫidûtu and rīštu, one Hebrew word per lemma.
šiptu; ēpišu; mehru (antiphon); irtu (a song type); zamāru קֶסֶם (settled 2026-10-21, §9); עוֹשֶׂה (כְּשָׁפִים); מַעֲנֶה; אִירְתוּם (transliterated: "breast-song"?); זִמֵּר / זֶמֶר [cognate] Reserved: שיר never in project 1 (the Song's own title); zamāru = זמר [cognate].

Source Hebrew Tag / Bible Notes
X-ra u₃-na(-a)-dug₄ (line 1 of a letter) אֶל X אֱמֹר: [equivalent] ↔ כֹּה תֹאמְרוּן לַאדֹנִי לְעֵשָׂו כֹּה אָמַר עַבְדְּךָ יַעֲקֹב (בראשית לב:ה) The opening formula (Akk. ana X qibī-ma). u₃-na-dug₄ is a prospective "when you have said to him".
Y(-e) na-ab-be₂-a (line 2) זֶה אֲשֶׁר Y אוֹמֵר: as above (Akk. umma Y-ma). Not כֹּה אָמַר, which would make the formula biblical.
a-ma-ru-kam (the last line) מַבּוּל הוּא! Literally "it is (a matter of) the flood": the idiom for "urgent". Footnoted once per project; amaru = מַבּוּל as in the flood corpus.
ama; ama ugu-ĝu₁₀; dumu ki aĝ₂ אֵם; אִמִּי יוֹלַדְתִּי; בֵּן אָהוּב ki aĝ₂ = אָהַב (= râmu)
kaskal; lu₂-kaš₄; ra-gaba; silim / silim-ma דֶּרֶךְ; רָץ; צִיר ★ (harmonization 2026-10-21; Prov 13:17); שָׁלוֹם (silim = Akk. šulmu, [cognate]) šulmu ↔ הֲשָׁלוֹם אֲבִיכֶם הַזָּקֵן (בראשית מג:כז)

4. Echo control for this corpus (read before drafting)

  1. The Song of Songs is the danger and the prize. Its vocabulary is the natural Hebrew of love poetry, so a translator who reaches for "the beautiful word" manufactures a parallel at every line. Rule: every Song-word in a > line must be licensed by its real Akkadian counterpart (§3.1, §5); the Song's other words go to the apparatus as [equivalent] / [divergence] / [absent]. The real cognates (dādu דּוֹד, dišpu דְּבַשׁ, šamnu שֶׁמֶן, šaptu שָׂפָה, šumēlu שְׂמֹאל, eršu עֶרֶשׂ, aḫātu אָחוֹת, kallatu כַּלָּה, rēʾû רוֹעֶה, ṣīḫtu צְחוֹק) are kept visible – they are findings.
  2. Proverbs and Qohelet likewise: מָשָׁל, חָכְמָה, כְּסִיל, תּוֹעֵבָה, צֶדֶק / צַדִּיק, רָשָׁע, הֶבֶל, יִרְאַת, מוּסָר, עֵצָה are not to be used for convenience; each is licensed or absent (§5). The "better … than" form is used only where the Sumerian has it.
  3. The letters and the patriarchal stories (family law, the mother, the brothers, the father's house, debt): render the Sumerian legal words with the law corpus's Hebrew (e₂ ad-da = בֵּית אָב [equivalent ↔ בראשית יב:א; לא:יד]); mark the overlap, do not build it.
  4. ETCSL's and Wasserman's English are rank 3 and have their own biblicisms ("righteousness", "abomination", "fool", "wise", "beloved", "garden"): check each against the transliteration (★ rule).

5. Reserved strings (never in a > line unless the source line has the licensing word; checked by kol_tools.py verify, niqqud stripped, against the transliteration and the ORACC normalization and lemmas of the line)

  • Never: שיר (project 1; in Sumerian only šir₃), שושנה, חבצלת, לבנון, מור, לבונה, נרד, כרכם, קנמון, צוף, משל (and משלי), צדק / צדיק / צדקה, הבל, יראת, מוסר, אלהים, שאול, עולם, מנעול, פרי (project 1).
  • Gated: דוד… ← dādu; the root אהב ← the râmu family / Sum. ki aĝ₂; צחק / צחוק ← ṣiāḫu / ṣīḫtu; תפוח ← ḫašḫūru / Sum. ḫašḫur; גן ← kirû / Sum. kiri₆; יונה ← summatu / Sum. tu-gur₄; דבש ← dišpu / Sum. lal₃; יין ← karānu / kurunnu / Sum. ĝeštin; שמן ← šamnu / Sum. i₃; כלה ★ ← kallatu / ḫīrtu / Sum. emi / e₂-gi₄-a; ערש ← eršu; משכב ← mayyālu / Sum. ki-nu₂; רעיה ← marḫītu; חבק ← ḫabābu; לפת ← edēru; נשק ← našāqu / kakku / Sum. ne … su-ub; שמאל ← šumēlu / Sum. gub₃; imperative קום… ← tebû / Sum. zig₃ / gana; לכה / לכי ← alāku / Sum. ĝen / du; בואי / בואה / בוא (imperative) ← erēbu / bâʾu / Sum. ku₄; חכמה / חכם ← nam-kug-zu / kug-zu / nēmequ; תועבה ← niĝ₂-gig / an-zil; רשע ← erim₂ / raggu; כסיל ← lil₂ / lillu; טוב ← dug₃ / du₁₀ / ṭābu; שוב / השיב ← gi₄ / gur / târu; ברך / ברכה ← karābu / ikribu / Sum. šud₃; ארר ← arāru / Sum. nam … ku₅; קלל / קללה ← Sum. aš₂ / Akk. arratu? (fixed: aš₂); נכרי / נכר ← Sum. kur₂ / nakru; עבד ← arad / wardu; אמה ★ (slave woman) ← geme₂ / amtu; מבול ← amaru / abūbu.

6. Traps of unvocalized Hebrew (checked where the name is in the source line)

אותו (Utu אוּתוּ), איננה (Inana אִינַנָּה), אור (Urim אוּר), אן (An אַן), אנו (Anu אָנוּ), סין (Sîn סִין), באו (Bau בָּאוּ), ארורו (Aruru אֲרוּרוּ), דוד / דודי / דודים (dādu: always vocalized), ציר / צירי (ra-gaba צִיר: unvocalized "birth pangs"), פוך / הפוך (šembi פּוּךְ: unvocalized "reversed"), כלה (bride: כַּלָּה), אמה (slave woman אָמָה; Umma; cubit), שנה (sleep שֵׁנָה / year שָׁנָה: vocalize where both are possible), אלי (my god אֵלִי), רעי (רֵעִי my friend / רַעְיִי), חם (father-in-law חָם / hot), אהבים (אֳהָבִים).

9. Merged from the runs

Project 1 (all 25 texts, 2026-10-21):

  • aḫāzu = אָחַז [cognate] (gated by script); ṣabātu = תָּפַס – a deviation from the Gilgameš corpus (ṣabātu = אחז), because this corpus has both and the Song's אֲחַזְתִּיו (שיר השירים ג:ד) must stay visible. A Sumerian dab₅ (= ṣabātu) takes תָּפַס.
  • mēlulu = שִׂחֵק (deviation from Gilgameš חוּל: here it takes an object); צחק stays reserved for ṣiāḫu.
  • ṣawāru "neck" = צַוָּאר [cognate]; šīnātu = שֶׁתֶן; sāqu = שׁוֹק [cognate]; warādu = יָרַד [cognate]; tamû D = הִשְׁבִּיעַ.
  • qadištu = קְדֵשָׁה, nadītu = נָדִיתוּ, kezertu = כְּזֵרָה, batultu = בְּתוּלָה (the law and Gilgameš corpora); šasû = צָעַק (Gilgameš); palāsu N = הִסְתַּכֵּל; ḫasāsu = הָגָה.
  • The incantation closing šiptum ul yâtu, šipat DN = הקסם אינו שלי: קסם DN.
  • One Hebrew verb per joy lemma: ḫadû שָׂמַח, riāšu גָּל, ḫašāšu שָׂשׂ, šâlu צָהַל, elēṣu עָלַץ.
  • The project's own words: 1-שירי-אהבה/renderings.md.

Project 2 (all 500 proverb lines, 2026-10-21):

  • The formula of 1.152–1.153, 3.9 is giri₁₇-zal-še₃ nu-il₂ = לששון – לא נשא (§3.2 corrected); niĝ₂-gig DN = תּוֹעֲבַת DN confirmed (3.118, 3.170, 3.171, 3.175), and without a god (1.23) תּוֹעֵבָה הִיא.
  • gu₂ = צַוָּאר (runs 5–6); kal = יָקָר; lu₂-kur₂ = אִישׁ נָכְרִי; dim₂ = עִצֵּב; uru₃ = נָצַר, en-nu-uĝ₃ = נְצִירָה; zid (of persons) = אִישׁ אֱמֶת; si sa₂ = יֹשֶׁר; zeb = עָרֵב, ku₇ = מָתוֹק, zil₂ = נָעִים; mu-ud-na = בֶּן־זוּג / בַּת־זוּג; gi₄-in = שִׁפְחָה; ḫu-ru-um = נִבְעָר; lu₂-ki-inim-ma = עֵד; ḫi-li = חֵן (= Akk. kuzbu, which project 1 renders עֲגָבִים: the Sumerian word is broader); e₂-dub-ba-a = בֵּית הַלּוּחוֹת.
  • The words עוֹלָם, צֶדֶק / צַדִּיק, כְּסִיל (without lil₂), מָשָׁל do not occur in the 500 lines. The project's own words: 2-משלים-שומריים/renderings.md.

Project 3 (all 178 letter lines, 2026-10-21):

  • The letter formulas confirmed and enforced: אֶל X אֱמֹר: (also when u₃-na-dug₄ stands alone on its line), זֶה אֲשֶׁר Y אוֹמֵר: / אוֹמֶרֶת:, the second address u₃-na-de₃-taḫ = הוֹסֵף:, a-ma-ru-kam = מַבּוּל הוּא!; 5.5.1's ĝiškim … ga-mu-ra-ab-šum₂ = אוֹת … אֶתֵּן לְךָ:.
  • gi₄ "send" = שָׁלַח, "return" = שׁוּב (by sense); ḫi-li = חֵן (also in the proverbs: changed from עֲגָבִים); zeb = עָרֵב, ku₇ = מָתוֹק; tukum-bi X an-na-kam = אִם רְצוֹן X הוּא; mu sa₄ = קָרָא שֵׁם (sa₄ = nabû); giĝ₄ / ma-na / gun₂ / sila₃ = שֶׁקֶל / מָנֶה / כִּכָּר / קַב. The project's own words: 3-מכתבים/renderings.md.

2026-10-21 harmonization (the lead's cross-corpus decisions, STATUS §6; one Hebrew per source word in all corpora): za-gin₃ = uqnû = סַפִּיר [equivalent] (was לָזוּרִית: LAOS 4 26 o.3, 3.3.01 1, 5.5.1 30; the note on Exod 24:10, Ezek 1:26, Job 28:6 at the first occurrence per text); šembi(zid) = פּוּךְ (was כָּחָל: proverb 1.150, D22; always vocalized, הפוך reads "the reverse"); ra-gaba = צִיר [equivalent ↔ Prov 13:17, 25:13], always vocalized (was רוכב (שליח): proverb 2.72, A129); šudu₃ = בְּרָכָה, sizkur₂ = תְּפִלָּה, a-ra-zu = תַּחֲנוּן (was תפילה: 3.3.10 6; šudu₃ was already ברכה, and the תחנונים of 3.3.10 5 is šag₄-ne-ša₄, kept); guru₇ = כְּרִי [cognate via karû] (was אסם: proverb 1.146, D14); en₃-du = זִמְרָה, number kept (זִמְרָתָהּ, was זמירותיה: proverb 1.70, B19); sukkallu = וְזִיר (was השר: LAOS 4 06 o.i.23); Inana אִינַנָּה everywhere, also in the apparatus (the plain אינאנה replaced). Kept (decided without edits): šiptu / tu₆ = קֶסֶם (the closing formula unchanged), ṣabātu = תָּפַס (this corpus has aḫāzu = אָחַז), niĝ₂-gig and an-zil both תּוֹעֵבָה, māru as endearment = בֵּן, uĝ₃ by sense, Dumuzi as is. Not affected here: šu-ur₂-men, nam-šub, mušen (only as a determinative), me, ur₄ "gather", kabattu (already כָּבֵד). Checked by kol_tools.py FORMULAS (the new Hebrew required where the source word is) and TRAPS (צִיר, פּוּךְ).

2026-10-23 harmonization (harmonization--2026-10-23.md row 18): nissatu = יָגוֹן, ašuštu = דַּאֲבוֹן; changed lines: LAOS 4 16 r.iv.9 ומעצב – אינה יתרה עליי. → ומדאבון – אינה יתרה עליי. (the table's ודאבון – אינו יתר עליי read ומעצב as the noun מַעֲצֵב; but u ašuštim still depends on eli of r.iv.8 – "more than sleeplessness and distress" – and the subject is אהבתך, so the comparative מ־ and the feminine אינה יתרה stay). No nissatu in this corpus.
